reviews.title: Love it!
reviews.text: I just downloaded this app, and love it so far! I enjoy the simplicity of it and that it’s not trying to be 1000 things at once. The UI is intuitive and pleasant to look at and I only have a few suggestions on how it could be better. The habits tracker: I love how easy it is to add new habits and give them a minimum unit. However, I wish there was an option to see your count for habits that you plan to do twice or multiple times a day. For example, if I want to meditate twice a day as my goal, I can only mark the goal as done when I’ve done both rather than when I’ve done the first one. I’m asking for this feature because if I check it off as I go along my day, I’m more likely to stick with the routine. Whereas if I do something in the morning but have to wait until that night to mark it, I’m more likely to forget about it. The focus timer: I wish we could do custom times. I love the design of it and that it counts the total time and has cycles, but everyone pomodoros differently. Using the meditation example again, if I only want to do 10 minutes I either have to do 5 or 15. While it’s workable, it’s not ideal and I end up getting off the app and using something else This is all I can think of for now but I am loving it so far!

reviews.title: Free and Simple
reviews.text: In short: it does what I want and helps me feel good about achieving those small or big habits in a simple way so I don’t get full of myself. In long: I feel like it’s up to date with functionality. It has a little feature of its own which has helped me stay on track with my goals even on the hard days and I can organize them how I want. I can also select if I want to track my “streak” or simply “number count” of how many times I’ve done it, for example there are some habits where I only need/want to do them 3 times a week, so the number count helps. Adding the quick overview of the week, I can see how I’m doing on those goals/habits. Overall a simple and easy and functional app that doesn’t give you too much-it gives the right amount on the right focus

reviews.title: Not bad
reviews.text: This app lets you to track as many habits as you want with no subscription and no ads, which is great. It’s easy to use, aesthetically pleasing, and does what it’s meant to do. I wish I could make certain goals only visible on certain days, or if they have not been met. Looking at the entire list every time is a bit overwhelming. I also wish the goal you set for yourself was visible from the main list, without having to click on the task to compare your target number of days to your actual progress. Or, better yet, if the colored rectangle served as a progress bar so you could see at a glance which goals you were closer/further from meeting. I found some decent workarounds though, using color-coding and the “define a smallest unit” field to make it better meet my needs. Would give 4.5 stars if I could.

reviews.title: Simple, easy, effective
reviews.text: I love this app, it has helped me to keep up with my vitamins and activity in a very simple way. I don’t like more complicated methods—you end up focusing on recording what you’re doing, instead of just doing it!! This is perfect for my needs. In an absolute dream world, you’d be able to change the units of time, so that instead of all habits being checked off once per day, you could check instead make a habit five times times per day. You can set it this way, but the graphics and streak calculator don’t really reflect it in a straightforward manner. Even without this feature, this is still the best app out there for what it does. Much thanks to the developer!

reviews.title: Soooo great!
reviews.text: This app is so great! I love how simple, easy to use, and nice looking it is! The one thing I would suggest is to look at the UI of the app "Atoms." and read Atomic Habits by james clear and try to implement some of the tips from that book in the app, like habit stacking. Also regarding "Atoms." I think your UI could really really benefit from a satisfying animation when you click off a habit like in Atoms so its satisfying when you complete a habit. Also, I think it would be more helpful to see each habit in a list per-DAY instead of per-WEEK, and rhen have a weekly view of habits and if youve completed/failed throughout the week, instead of having that on the main habit checklist menu. That way #1 its easier to make it satisfying to complete the habit cause it can take up the whole card/screen, and #2 it makes it nicer for users cause you can see just that day instead of worrying about the whole week! Okay thanks love it guys!!! keep it up!!! ALSO I LOVE THAT THIS APP IS FREE!! WOO!! ================= ALSO: you should open source this!!! I'd love to be a contributor to such a great project!! =================

reviews.title: The perfect habit tracker

As someone who struggles with making subscription payments, and honestly just commitments of any sort, this app is super minimal and free; there are no ads there are no hidden subscriptions or no in app, purchases that are needed to be made to access all of the features. reviews.title: Love the colorful, simple interface. Missing a few key functionalities.
reviews.text: I’ve used a few habit tracking apps and this is my favorite interface that I’ve seen. I love that it’s clean, colorful and easy to read. Great work! Would love to keep using it but definitely missing a few functions that I’ve seen in other apps that would be useful: - Being able to check off a habit multiple times in one day (for instance, for medicine that needs to be taken morning and night) - Being able to duplicate already created habits so as not to have to set all parameters from scratch - Being able to click through the calendar to see habit/task lists on different days - Being able to sort habits by time of day (morning vs evening for example) - Being able to set the time increment to “weeks” or “months” for habits. Currently, everything is by days so a weekly habit must be set to every “7 days”, which isn’t totally intuitive.
